intro: At Seferihisar, in İzmir province, lie the remains of the Ancient City of Teos. This Ionian city's story reaches back to the 11th century BC, and it was home to the largest Temple of Dionysos in the ancient world.
history: Teos was founded in the 11th–10th century BC and became one of the twelve cities of the Ionian League. In the 6th century BC it fell to Persia, and some of its citizens fled to found Abdera in 543 BC. In the Hellenistic period the city came under Pergamon, and in the late 3rd century BC it hosted the Guild of Dionysiac Artists. Even in Roman times, Teos kept its importance.
structure-1: Now you are standing before the Temple of Dionysos, dedicated to the god of wine. Pause for a moment and picture the god who was honoured here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the theatre and the odeon, then the bouleuterion, and finally the agora.
facts: Did you know? The Guild of Dionysiac Artists (Technitai Dionysou) organised here, the first known guild of actors, poets and musicians — a professional union, perhaps the ancient world's first. The city's Temple of Dionysos is the largest temple to the god known from the ancient world. And Anacreon, the poet of wine and love, came from this very city.
outro: This brings our journey through the Ancient City of Teos to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
